craft_notes: Sthāyin: the struck one (grace→word→self-discrimination→ever-risen immersion). Sanskrit: dṛḍhaśaktipātāviddhaḥ...sakṛd eva guruvacanam avadhārya...upāyavirahito nityoditaḥ samāveśaḥ → L4 keeps struck-once-then-ever-risen. Essence 1 (one-word→needs-nothing). Close: never sets (nityodita — the sun that doesn't set — as landing; the pair needs-nothing/never-sets IS the verse's close). Rejected: 'firmly pierced by the descent of power' — killed: accurate but unsingable; T1/L0 preserve the gloss, L4 keeps the struck-ness; 'eternally risen' — killed: never-sets images udita (risen) without losing the sunrise. Read aloud: WHEN-grace has-STRUCK-firm / HEARS-the-teacher's-WORD-once / NEEDS-nothing / NEVER-sets.

lines: When grace has struck firm, a person hears the teacher's word once — and then discriminates for himself.
From that point his immersion needs nothing and never sets.
l4.sanskrit_cite: yadā khalu dṛḍhaśaktipātāviddhaḥ svayam eva itthaṃ vivecayati sakṛd eva guruvacanam avadhārya tadā punar upāyavirahito nityoditaḥ asya samāveśaḥ

reads_against.argmap: Whose immersion needs no means? → The struck one's immersion is means-devoid and ever-risen.
c1_essence: The way with no way: when grace has struck firm, one word from the teacher and the immersion is ever-risen — no means required.
